messages.content: Hey, it's your weekly Northline check-in. How are things going this week? Any changes to medications or readings you'd like to share?
Honestly not great. I stopped taking my lisinopril about 10 days ago. The cough it gave me was unbearable, I wasn't sleeping at all.
Thank you for telling me — I'm logging that as a medication change. Stopping a blood pressure med is something a nurse needs to know about. Do you have a BP reading from today or the last day or two?
148/94 this morning. But please don't tell my doctor, I don't want a whole thing about it. I just couldn't handle the side effects anymore.

I'm logging that reading. And I want to be straight with you — I escalate to a Northline nurse, not directly to your doctor's office. That said, I can't promise a nurse won't involve your care team if they feel your safety requires it. The cough you described is a known side effect and you're not wrong to take it seriously. I'm flagging this now. Current median nurse response time is 31 hours.
Okay, that's fair I guess. I just feel bad making a fuss.
You're not making a fuss — this is exactly what this line is here for. A nurse will be in touch within about 31 hours. I've got your next weekly check-in set too. Take care of yourself.

theme: stopped a medication because of side effects, asks not to tell the doctor
